costs.measuredOn: the same host, one process per leg, one request per cell; wireBytes is what the server wrote on the socket

decisionInput.dependencyCost: a pure-Go brotli encoder is a NEW module dependency (the standard library has none); the project rule is no new CI dependency without approval, and the provider transport additionally needs a DECODER before the client may advertise br upstream.
decisionInput.gotavern_behaviour: GoTavern compression.go supports gzip/deflate from the standard library; it deliberately does NOT advertise or produce brotli because the standard library has neither encoder nor decoder, and the CORS-proxy/provider paths would otherwise advertise an encoding they cannot read.
decisionInput.pinned_behaviour: pinned compresses with the npm `compression` middleware (src/server-main.js:107, app.use(compression())). For a browser-like Accept-Encoding the negotiated encoding is br on compressible bodies at/over the 1024-byte threshold; the exact per-resource outcome is in the pinnedLeg rows.
decisionInput.userVisibleCost: a modern browser receives gzip from GoTavern where pinned sends br; the decoded bytes are identical, so the cost is bandwidth on large static assets, quantified in brotliVsGzip above.

method.client: node:http raw request (NOT fetch): undici would decompress gzip/br and hide the selected encoding
method.csrf: GET /csrf-token before each leg, to confirm the leg speaks the product contract; the GETs themselves need no token

purpose: capture the pinned Content-Encoding negotiation and representation sizes for real browser Accept-Encoding values, and the same surface on GoTavern, to decide the Brotli cost/benefit from measured bytes
unproven: No throughput/CPU measurement: this probe measures representation size, not compression cost. A perf claim belongs to the perf lane.
One host, one run per cell; the wire sizes are deterministic for a fixed asset+codec but the elapsedMs is not evidence of anything.

verdicts.evidence: pinnedLeg rows: the same resource, same path, different Accept-Encoding produces different Content-Encoding and different wire bytes
comparison[].representationIdentityMatch: decoded representations are the same bytes across encodings and subjects (a false here would be a different asset, not a codec)

comparison rows where encodingDifference is true; gotavern answers the standard-library encodings only. This is the exact difference the alpha.19 release disclosed; this probe measures its size instead of describing it.
brotliVsGzip shows the bytes a browser saves; implementing it needs a new dependency plus a decoder on the outbound transport, so it stays a Lead decision, not a probe conclusion
